newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi endorses investment deal with Germany.
newsitem.headline: Saudi endorses investment deal with Germany.

text.p: The Saudi Arabian government on Monday endorsed an investment protection agreement with Germany to foster bilateral economic ties, the official Saudi news agency SPA said.
The deal was signed in principle in October but had to be reviewed by the kingdom's Shura consultative council before the government endorsed it at Monday's weekly session which King Fahd chaired.
Germany is Saudi Arabia's fourth largest trading partner, while the kingdom is Germany's top trading partner in the Arab world.
Both countries agreed to boost economic, trade, commercial and investment co-operation during meetings in Riyadh in March of a German-Saudi joint commission on economic and technical co-operation.
Bonn has long urged Riyadh to improve investment conditions in the kingdom to boost bilateral trade.

Total bilateral trade figures between Germany and Saudi Arabia stood at around 4.8 billion marks ($2.8 billion) in 1995, down from 5.7 billion marks in 1994, according to German embassy figures. In the first nine months of 1996 it stood at 3.7 billion marks.
